classification.reason: SIC 6021 is a depository institution (SIC 6000-699x) — DCF/NOPAT-based valuation is structurally unsuitable for a bank, by construction, not because of any data gap: for a bank, debt/leverage IS the business model (deposits and borrowings fund the loan book), not a financing choice layered on top of an operating business the way the EV bridge (lib/analyzer/modules/enterpriseValue.ts) assumes for every other golden company. The engine must refuse JPM outright, not force a NOPAT/EV number out of a bank. classifyCyclicality('6021') itself returns 'stable' (no confirmed cyclical SIC prefix matches 6021) — that literal table output is NOT what drives the refusal; refused=true is a separate, structural, bank-specific override, confirmed here only as a documentation fact, not read from cyclicalSic.ts.

revenue.note: CAPTURED BUT NOT A DCF-COMPARABLE 'REVENUE' — this is JPM's own structural-absence golden fact. us-gaap:Revenues is present with a real, current value, so this is NOT simply a missing tag; but the XBRL element's own official description (read directly from the real capture's tag metadata) is: 'Amount of revenue recognized from goods sold, services rendered, insurance premiums, or other activities... Includes... investment and interest income before deduction of interest expense when recognized as a component of revenue, and sales and trading gain (loss).' That is total net revenue for a bank (net interest income + noninterest revenue, gross of interest expense netting conventions specific to banks) — structurally not the same concept as a product/service company's net sales that reverseDcf.ts's baseYearRevenue assumes. This is the real, data-grounded basis for refusing JPM: not an absent tag, a present tag that means something categorically different for a depository institution.

facts.operatingIncomeNote: us-gaap:OperatingIncomeLoss is entirely absent from JPM's real captured facts — banks do not report operating income the way a non-financial company does (interest expense is netted against interest income before arriving at net revenue, not treated as a financing cost below an operating line).

facts.totalDebtNote: DELIBERATELY NOT COMPUTED — not a data gap, a structural one. For a depository institution, 'total debt' in the non-financial-company EV-bridge sense (lib/analyzer/modules/enterpriseValue.ts: debt + leases − cash, added to market cap) has no coherent meaning: JPM's balance sheet is dominated by deposits and trading liabilities that ARE its funding model, not discretionary financing layered over an operating business. Observed anyway, for completeness, as a second real tag-drift instance (bonus, not asserted by tagDrift.test.ts): us-gaap:LongTermDebt is dead for JPM (last 10-K row FY2013, 267889000000); us-gaap:LongTermDebtNoncurrent/Current are entirely absent; us-gaap:ShortTermBorrowings is live (FY2025, 64776000000) but is only one small component of a bank's real funding stack (deposits, long-term debt issued through other disclosures, trading liabilities — none of which this harness attempts to reconstruct, since no engine total-debt figure should be computed for a refused company in the first place).
